proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a matched whole-record logarithmic frontier for benchmark risk, exactly 90%-honest connected length and the endpoint modulus, plus unrestricted published-class risk/length lower bounds of 1/2 and 0.90. Independent informal consults and four cited-source checks support the mathematics, but D0.5 capped the achieved tier to incremental (5.8 below field 7.4), leaving a redundant density-envelope finding unrepaired. No F-stage Lean formalization, source/axiom audit or Lean certification occurred; the wider compact-mixing class is preserved as a future re-anchor, with runtime and finite-sample practical precision unestablished.
tldr: The known Gaussian NIR formula identifies the observed-cutoff contrast as a noise-weighted causal effect. Over the self-defined near-uniform interior benchmark \(\mathcal M\), the matched original-record minimax absolute-risk and finite-sample \(0.90\)-honest connected expected-length frontier is \(r_n=n^{-1/2}[1+\log n/\log(2+\log n)]^{3/4}\), with an evaluated complete-record modulus and certified data-only attainment for every \(n\ge2\). The benchmark fixes one public unit-Gaussian precision, an unknown density on \([-1,1]\) between \(1/4\) and \(3/4\), and arbitrary Borel Bernoulli means between \(1/4\) and \(3/4\). Unrestricted published binary unit-Gaussian \(\mathcal N\) instead satisfies \(R_n^{\mathcal N}\ge1/2\) and \(H_n^{\mathcal N}\ge9/10\) for every \(n\ge2\). Endpoint rare-treatment pairs and a continuum of response probabilities prove these exact same-family limiting lower bounds using every original score and mark and arbitrary independent randomization. The weaker benchmark converse also transfers by strict inclusion. Matching, upper modulus evaluation and certified attainment remain benchmark guarantees.
gap: NIR Example 3 identifies the observed-cutoff contrast on a broader class. The verified linear mixture-duality theorem leaves its modulus to be evaluated and does not directly apply to the nonlinear unknown-denominator ratio. Exact final-journal theorem comparison is externally unverifiable.
